note: Independently re-judged from the full RFC 4271 Section 8.2.2 OpenConfirm list and RFC 6608 Section 4. TestRFC4271OpenConfirmUpdateIsAnFSMError sends an empty UPDATE (Event 27) and the retained withdrawn-length overrun (Event 28) after OPEN and before KEEPALIVE. Each requires exactly one 5/2, TCP closure, three stopped session timers, session release and counter 0 to 1. The close helper distinguishes closure from a read deadline but does not require the concrete io.EOF value. updateIsUnexpected intercepts these inputs before UPDATE semantic parsing, and fsmMessageEvent preserves the receiving state for the RFC 6608 response; the shared FSM catchall still performs the listed counter/state actions. TestRFC4271ExpectedMessagesRaiseNoFSMError gives a conforming OpenConfirm KEEPALIVE that reaches Established and the same empty UPDATE accepted there, retaining connection/session and counter zero. Native renewals for the positive and existing boundary controls are green before their named producer breaks and red under those breaks; reverts establish dependence, not every possible fault. The updater changes the diagnostic subcode to 2 while the original teardown obligations remain. No separate credit is claimed here for RFC 6608's one-octet message Data.
